# BTicino C300X Integration v2.10.0

## Unreleased

[![Support me on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/img/githubbutton_sm.svg)](https://ko-fi.com/oliver7557)

2.10.0 adds firmware 3.0.6 (Classe 300X hardware revision 4) to 1.7.x and
2.0.2. Everything below is new against 2.9.2.

A 3.0.6 station gets the display pages with the agent update, also when it
comes from 2.9.2. On a 3.0.6 station a tester checked that the display pages
load at start and that the Alarm and Home Assistant buttons sit in the right
place; the rest of the 3.0.6 support is checked offline only, with the
station's own display components and shell. A display that crashes with the
pages starts as shipped; one that hangs with them instead was not seen on a
station and is not caught: the station then restarts again and again, and
the way out is the SSH steps at the end of these notes.

## Firmware 3.0.6

- The **Display patch** works on 3.0.6, whose display program carries its
  pages inside itself. The station gets the same pages as on 1.7.x and 2.0.2:
  the **Alarm** and **Home Assistant** buttons with the house symbol on the
  home page, the Alarm, Home Assistant and Energy pages and the
  **Integration** tab in the station's **Settings**. **Home page buttons**
  offers **Stock** and **Fixed side by side** here too. The fix for lost taps
  is not part of it on 3.0.6.
- The display restarts after a change one restart at a time and only after
  the old display has ended; several changes close together end in one
  restart. A restart that takes longer than a request is reported as running
  (`gui_restart: pending`), and Home Assistant and the installers wait for
  its outcome instead of reporting a failure.
- A display that fails with the pages is restarted once more and then starts
  as shipped until the station restarts; the patch status reads **applied,
  but the display started as shipped**. Turning the **Display patch** switch
  on, the core hook Repair or an agent update tries the pages again; saving
  the display settings does not.
- A display step that fails during an install from Home Assistant or an agent
  update no longer fails the install or update: the step stays owed, and the
  core hook Repair stays until it has run again. A step that could not run at
  all (no connection, agent busy, rejected key) still fails.
- The agent knows the display program of firmware 3.0.6. On another build
  it applies the pages only when it finds exactly one matching set of pages
  in the program and the start script is the original one of 3.0.6;
  otherwise the display stays as shipped, the agent runs without the display
  pages and Repairs says why.
- The camera's stream on 3.0.6 offers the sizes 320x240, 352x288, 400x288
  (factory), 480x288, 640x384, 640x480, 704x576, 720x432 and 720x576. Sizes
  other than the factory one are not yet tested on a station.

## Station (all firmwares)

- The **Integration** tab is laid out as one aligned column. A long address
  breaks only after a dot or a colon and keeps its start and its port in
  view; the row is called **Address**. A message of the tab (a setting
  not saved, SSH, restart, removal) shows at the foot of the tab, where it
  stays in view, instead of at the end of the page.
- **Energy**: the hour labels of the **Today** view sit below the bars, and
  the flow arrows stay on their lines in every direction.
- The consumers view of the Energy page is kept while the notification list
  or the **More** list covers it: the bars are not built again and the
  scales do not jump when the list closes.
- A display notification no longer shows a black band above its button, and
  its message area ends on a whole line.
- Opening a dashboard page no longer writes two warnings into the station's
  log.

## Home Assistant and agent

- **Save images** shows the cause of its last failure in words; the
  attribute `last_failure` keeps its codes for automations and is absent
  while images succeed.
- A visitor image that is stored after the capture's time limit counts as
  saved: it becomes the preview and is linked to the visit.
- A display restart or a display repair that runs past its time limit
  finishes instead of leaving the display off, and Home Assistant waits for
  its answer. A write of the media-user label that hangs ends after its time
  limit and is rolled back, and the agent stays responsive meanwhile. A
  display step of the SSH install that runs past its time limit is rolled
  back on the station.
- A repair that was confirmed finishes even when the browser tab closes or
  the connection drops meanwhile, the agent update with its reload included.
  When Home Assistant stops while the station applies an agent update, the
  next start still offers the repair that brings the display pages back.
- The native agent is rebuilt as 2.10.0; an agent update is required.

## Short Test List for 3.0.6 Stations

1. Full install of 2.10.0 from Home Assistant, or the agent update. Pages
   active, no `display-qt5.rcc.failed`, no core hook Repair left.
2. Open **Settings > Integration**: the status block shows Home Assistant as
   reachable, the address, the last contact and the three versions. Switch
   the page change and **Keep page open in standby** once each and back; the
   integration's options show the same.
3. Tap **Reboot station**, then **No**: the window closes, nothing happens.
4. On the home page the house symbol sits beside the power button. Stop Home
   Assistant: within five minutes it gets the yellow mark and a tap opens
   **Settings > Integration** with the reason. Start Home Assistant again:
   the Alarm and Home Assistant buttons come back by themselves.
5. Press Reload three times quickly, then save the display settings twice.
   Exactly one display at the end, no watchdog reboot, overlay still active.
6. Full removal (`restore-all`): stock start script back, `qt5_overlay: off`.
7. Reboot with the overlay active. Pages come up, no boot loop.

If the station keeps restarting after an install, an update or saving the
display settings:

1. Over SSH, between two restarts, rename the display resource file:
   `mv /home/bticino/cfg/extra/c300x-native-agent/display-qt5.rcc /home/bticino/cfg/extra/c300x-native-agent/display-qt5.rcc.hang`.
   The next start uses the original display.
2. Once the original display runs, remove the pages and the core hook over
   SSH: `/home/bticino/cfg/extra/c300x-native-agent/qml_patch.sh restore-all`.
   Its last line contains `"qt5_overlay":"off"`; the display restarts once, as
   shipped. If it answers `An unfinished GUI write is still in place`, wait a
   minute and run it again.
3. If the restarts began with an install from Home Assistant or after saving
   the display settings, also turn off **Home Assistant pages on the display**
   (this discards the page settings); otherwise Home Assistant applies the
   pages again at its next start. After step 2 this writes nothing to the
   station.
4. Until you have reported it, do not run the core hook Repair, the
   **Display patch** switch or an agent update: each writes the resource file
   again. Report the Display patch status, the integration diagnostics and
   `/tmp/c300x-display-qt5.log`, and keep `display-qt5.rcc.hang`.

## Still Unverified on a Station

- When the display first writes its watchdog file on a cold start and how
  often it writes it, and the gap between the old display's last write and
  the new one's first during a Reload. The 40 s and 8 s limits rest on this.
- How long the first display write after an install or update takes on
  3.0.6 before it asks for the display restart (reading the original pages
  and packing the new ones); it must stay within the 30 s limit of a display
  write.
- Whether `pidof BtClass` ever shows a second PID while the display runs.
- Every station page on the 3.0.6 display, with touch.

## Upgrade

The agent-update Repair installs the 2.10.0 agent together with its display
files. The changes under **Station** need the optional Display patch.

Before returning a 3.0.6 station to a release without 3.0.6 support (2.9.x
or older), fully remove its display overlay with `qml_patch.sh restore-all`
and confirm the stock display start and `qt5_overlay: off`. Older releases
cannot remove it.
